rounds.text: Rishabh Instruments Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 25% over 5 years and an extraordinary 78% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E19]. Operating efficiency is expanding visibly, with operating margin rising to 23% in March 2026—a 7 percentage point increase over three years [E24]. Financial health is exceptionally robust, as the company remains almost debt free with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and profits backed strongly by a cash conversion rate of 1.38x [E28, E32, E53]. Furthermore, heavy capital expenditure is actively underway to fuel future expansion, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress surging by 266.7% to Rs 44 Cr in March 2026 [E34]. Market participation confirms underlying strength, featuring a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a twelve-month price return of 109.2%, and positive institutional money flow [E38, E45, E46]. Conceded: [E39], [E40], [E41], [E55], [E56].

Rishabh Instruments Ltd trades at an expensive valuation that is disconnected from its underlying return profile, carrying a P/E ratio of 57.8x and a price-to-book multiple of 5.24x [E1, E2, E55]. A discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 443 per share against a market price of Rs 624, resulting in a severe margin of safety of -41.0% [E39, E40]. Furthermore, the current price already demands 22.8% earnings growth, surpassing the base-case assumption of 18.0% [E41]. Operating margins remain inconsistent over the last two years and trailing three quarters [E26, E27], while historical returns on equity are modest with a 5-year median of 8% and a 3-year figure of 9% [E21, E22, E56]. Institutional backing is also retreating as domestic institutional holdings dropped from 16.55% in Sep 2023 to 11.21% in Jun 2026, and foreign holdings declined from 1.66% to 1.17% over the same timeframe [E36, E37]. Conceded: [E20]
